studies.label: Marketing-campaign experiment (generic, personalized, and partially personalized GPT-4o assistant)

arms.name: Generic AI
arms.description: GPT-4o assistant at temperature 1, with the company description and initial campaign idea; asks focused questions, builds on contributions, and gives feedback, without a personal profile (PDF pp. 21-22; PDF p. 37, printed supplement p. 9).

arms.name: Personalized AI
arms.description: Same assistant with the participant’s psychological, cognitive, and demographic profile and a summary of an AI-guided interview about marketing experience and collaborative work style (PDF pp. 21-22; PDF p. 38, printed supplement p. 10).

arms.name: Partially personalized AI
arms.description: Same personalized assistant supplied with another participant’s profile and interview summary (PDF p. 22).

studies.task: Develop a marketing-campaign plan for Cultivated, a fictional lab-grown ribeye startup, covering product positioning, audience, messaging, channels, and success metrics (PDF p. 21; PDF p. 37, printed supplement p. 9).

estimates.outcome: Campaign quality, expert-human pairwise Elo (random validation sample)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Expert Prolific raters working in management, consulting, or market research compared overall campaign quality in pairs. An Elo score was assigned to each campaign in a randomly selected validation subset from the Generic AI and Personalized AI arms (PDF p. 32, printed supplement p. 4).

regression.model: Reported treatment coefficient for expert-human campaign Elo quality. Marketing skills are also analyzed. The estimator and full covariate specification are not printed for this validation analysis; adjustment for message count cannot be confirmed.

sources.locator: PDF p. 32 (printed supplement p. 4), Sensitivity Analyses, expert-human validation
sources.quote: We randomly selected a subset of 100 marketing campaigns, restricting our comparison to only generic or personalized AI.

sources.locator: PDF p. 32 (printed supplement p. 4), Sensitivity Analyses, expert-human validation
sources.quote: We find that there is no significant difference between treatment conditions (β = 158.2, p = 0.14), although the results are directionally correct, i.e., personalization leads to slightly higher Elo ratings.

estimates.notes: Retained as the contrast across the entire available randomly selected expert-rating sample, rather than an outcome- or characteristic-selected subgroup. This is not the entire experiment: the printed count is campaigns, so n_units is populated and person counts remain null. Raters are not randomized campaign-producing participants. Each person produced one final campaign; the regression outcome is its Elo score, supporting participant as the analysis basis. No arm split, arm means, SDs, SE, or interval is printed. The paper does not give this regression’s full adjustment set; this is an unresolved eligibility detail, not an assertion that it is unadjusted. The explicitly turn-adjusted LLM models are separately excluded.

estimates.outcome: Campaign theme diversity relative to the pooled campaign centroid (paper: creativity)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: GPT-4o extracts distinctive campaign themes, which are embedded with OpenAI text-embedding-3-large. Each campaign is compared with the mean embedding of all campaigns across treatment conditions (PDF p. 23; theme-extraction prompt, PDF p. 40, printed supplement p. 12). The results describe higher printed creativity scores as less homogeneous, although Methods calls the underlying measure cosine similarity. The transformation is unspecified.

estimates.outcome: Words differing between final campaign and the AI-suggested campaign (percentage)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: The supplement compares the words in the final submitted campaign with the AI assistant’s suggested campaign. The text does not name an overlap algorithm or say whether percentages average campaigns or pool words (PDF pp. 50-51, printed supplement pp. 22-23).

sources.locator: PDF p. 51 (printed supplement p. 23), Personalization Shifted Conversations from Collaborative to Strategic
sources.quote: Approximately 80.5% of words were different between the final campaign and what their AI assistant recommended versus 64.5% in the personalized arm.

estimates.notes: The preceding sentence on PDF p. 50 (printed supplement p. 22) identifies Generic AI users as those editing more before submission. Values are the printed arm-level percentages, with no conversion to proportions; the source introduces the comparison as approximate. Mean fields store these descriptive arm levels without claiming that the paper averaged participant scores. Aggregation unit, analyzed sample counts, and all uncertainty are unreported. Higher values mean more lexical change from the AI suggestion; no creativity or diversity direction is implied. This compares each person’s final campaign with its AI draft, not different people, so it is with_ai/other rather than across_people/diversity. It is scored on the submitted output and is retained under the codebook’s other construct; it must never be pooled. No partial-personalization percentage is reported.

open_items: Pre-exclusion randomized totals and exclusions by arm are not stated. The arm sizes are the analyzed sample after exclusions, despite the prose calling those people randomized (PDF p. 19).

Prospective preregistration timing and the prespecified primary-outcome hierarchy are not established by the saved manuscript. The supplied citation record documents an associated registration and amendment, but does not establish the data-collection timeline (PDF p. 19).

The mapping from theme cosine similarity to the printed creativity scale is not given; the results say higher scores mean less homogeneous campaigns. Whether autonomous AI-only campaigns enter the common centroid is unspecified (PDF pp. 10, 23).

The construction of the diversity arm confidence intervals and handling of common-centroid dependence are not explained. The analysis has one campaign score per participant (PDF pp. 21, 23). No full-sample pairwise treatment coefficient, test, or contrast uncertainty is printed (PDF p. 10).

The expert-human Elo validation does not report participant counts, an arm split, arm means/SDs, coefficient SE, or the full regression formula. It is unknown whether this model also adjusted for post-treatment message count; if confirmed, extraction rule 5 would require moving it to not_extracted (PDF p. 32, printed supplement p. 4).

The campaign-length regressions do not state their estimator or covariate set and do not print arm-level means/SDs or coefficient SEs. A pooled-sample word-count SD is not an arm-specific standardizer (PDF p. 19).

The final-campaign word-change percentages lack a named lexical metric, aggregation rule, analysis counts, uncertainty, and a partially personalized arm level (PDF pp. 50-51, printed supplement pp. 22-23).

Unadjusted LLM campaign-quality arm statistics or treatment contrasts would be needed to extract that outcome under the post-treatment-adjustment rule. The excluded LLM Elo analysis also has inconsistent personalized-arm p-values between main/supplement text and the figure caption (PDF pp. 7, 32, 53).
notes:
Reconciled on 2026-10-11. Read the complete markdown conversion, including all supplementary material and final references. Extracted the cited PDF pages with PyMuPDF and checked Tables S2, S3, and S5 with find_tables(). Every retained numeric-source quote was matched to its PDF page after whitespace normalization. No effect, difference, SD, SE, sample total, or figure value was computed. The script lists two study-field differences and no estimate-value differences or one-sided estimates. The resolutions also document two equivalent slug spellings. All estimates match between A and B; no new estimate absent from both was added. Every screened outcome and contrast is retained or covered by not_extracted. The source citation record resolves the older screening form’s version uncertainty through the verified file fingerprint. 

Agreement audit: the retained counts, question, construct, unit, higher_is, outcome_with_ai, and within_person were independently checked. PDF p. 19 and Table S2 establish analyzed people; pre-exclusion allocation totals remain null. Recruitment totals and expert raters are not substituted for randomized campaign-producing people. No two-arm totals are computed, and the expert-validation count remains n_units because the paper counts campaigns. PDF pp. 5 and 21-22 establish a between-person experiment with AI available during campaign production, so all within_person values are null and outcome_with_ai is true. Each person produces one final campaign; the Elo and length analyses use that output, not individual ratings. PDF p. 32 supports expert-rated usefulness; PDF pp. 10 and 23 support across_people/diversity and higher_is more_diverse for comparison with the pooled centroid. Word count is elaboration measured by length; its direction is other because more words do not necessarily mean more creative work. Final-word changes compare the submitted output with its own AI draft, so they are with_ai/other, not diversity; the aggregation unit remains unspecified. 

The main LLM quality regressions, robustness variants, and LLM Elo analysis control post-treatment turn count and are excluded. Quality-tertile results are excluded subgroups. Expert validation is a random measurement sample; its complete available contrast is retained, with its unspecified covariates flagged as an unresolved eligibility detail. Extra stats.control_ci_lower/control_ci_upper/control_ci_level fields preserve both printed diversity arm intervals without treating either as contrast uncertainty. The common-centroid CI method remains unclear. The final-output editing percentages were already present in both extractions despite being absent from the screening form, and must never be pooled as creativity. No cross-paper sample overlap is stated; expert validation and the autonomous benchmark reuse S1 campaigns. No direct Personalized AI versus Partially personalized AI contrast on final-campaign outcomes is separately printed. Both personalized-versus-generic comparisons share the Generic AI control arm.

fixes.quote: We operationalized each campaign’s creativity as the cosine similarity between its unique themes and the average text embedding of all campaigns across treatment conditions.
fixes.basis: The verifier flag is correct. PDF p. 21 assigns each participant a single campaign, p. 23 defines one creativity score for each campaign, and p. 10 reports arm means and confidence intervals. The extraction-spec.md se_basis field notes explicitly classify an analysis with one output per person as participant. The unreported CI formula and possible dependence through the common centroid do not make the observation basis unknown. No contrast SE or other statistic is inferred.

fixes.old: Full-sample arm summaries, not the quality-tertile regressions. No full-sample human-arm contrast coefficient, contrast CI, test, or p-value is printed; overlapping arm CIs are not treated as a test of no difference. No difference or SE has been computed. The printed CI in ci_lower/ci_upper concerns the treatment mean; the additional control_ci_* keys preserve the printed control-arm CI. CI computation and treatment of dependence through the shared centroid are not described, so se_basis is unclear. The centroid pools treatment conditions and this is not a pure within-arm dispersion measure. Inclusion of autonomous AI benchmark campaigns in the centroid is unspecified. The outcome is one score per campaign, with one campaign per person. General analyzed arm counts are from Table S2; no contrast-specific total or output count is printed, so those fields remain null. Direction follows the explicit interpretation on PDF p. 10 rather than reversing the printed scale.

CI computation and treatment of dependence through the shared centroid are not described. The arm intervals summarize one campaign score per participant, so se_basis is participant (PDF pp. 21, 23); the missing CI method and shared-centroid dependence remain methodological limitations. The centroid pools treatment conditions and this is not a pure within-arm dispersion measure. Inclusion of autonomous AI benchmark campaigns in the centroid is unspecified. The outcome is one score per campaign, with one campaign per person. General analyzed arm counts are from Table S2; no contrast-specific total or output count is printed, so those fields remain null. Direction follows the explicit interpretation on PDF p. 10 rather than reversing the printed scale.
